title: Conjugacy of generic-to-closed geometric specializations
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian excellent normal integral henselian local scheme with closed point $s$ and generic point $\eta$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Geometric points are spectra of chosen algebraic closures of residue fields [def-weil-geometric-point]. For geometric points $\bar\eta$ and $\bar s$ over $\eta,s$, a geometric specialization $t:\bar\eta\rightsquigarrow\bar s$ means an $S$-map $S_{(\bar\eta)}\to S_{(\bar s)}$ of strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Such specializations exist. If $t,t'$ are two of them, there is an $\eta$-automorphism $\sigma$ of $\bar\eta$ such that $t'=t\circ\sigma$. For every $s$-automorphism $\tau$ of $\bar s$ and every such $t$, there is an $\eta$-automorphism $\sigma$ of $\bar\eta$ such that $\tau\circ t=t\circ\sigma$, with composition interpreted on strict localizations. These assertions also hold for two different chosen geometric generic points, replacing $\sigma$ by an isomorphism between them.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.8 (the conjugating geometric isomorphisms) and Proposition 3.6.1 (generic Galois invariance); normality makes the strict localization integral

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$, and $\bar\eta=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}\Xi$. Let $K^s\subset\Omega$ and $k^s\subset\Xi$ be the separable algebraic closures of $K$ and $k=\kappa(s)$ inside the chosen algebraic closures, as in [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Put $B=A^{sh}_{\bar s}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](3) (with $U=S$), the colimit defining $B$ in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] is canonically the triples colimit of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] for $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$ and $k^s$, so $B$ is a local filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras, is strictly henselian, and has residue field $k^s$; the residue identification with $k^s\subset\Xi$ is [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). The same two results at the zero prime, with $\kappa(\bar\eta)=K^s$, identify $S_{(\bar\eta)}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}K^s$ over $S$: its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak pC=0$, and its residue map is an isomorphism to $K^s$. Normality of $A$ and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain](a),(b) show that $B$ is a domain and $A\to B$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 06DI, lemma-henselization-normal; Algebra Tags 04GW/04GP, strict henselization by triples; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), translation of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods into triples

proof.text: Let $C=(A\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B=B\otimes_AK$, a nonzero domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], the presentation in Step 1 makes $C/K$ ind-etale and hence weakly etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], every finitely generated $K$-subalgebra $D\subset C$ is finite etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], $D$ is a finite product of finite separable fields. Since $D$ is a nonzero subring of the domain $C$, it has no nontrivial idempotent, so this product has exactly one factor. In particular, every nonzero $c\in C$ has its inverse in the field $K[c]\subset C$. Thus $C$ is a field, necessarily $F=\operatorname{Frac}B$. The residue-field clause of [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] at the zero prime says $F/K$ is separable algebraic. Consequently every $A$-map $B\to K^s$ extends uniquely to a $K$-embedding $F\to K^s$, since it first factors through $C$, which is a field; conversely any such embedding restricts to an $A$-map. This describes exactly the specialization maps of the statement, by contravariance of affine spectra.

source.place: Tag 092Q, lemma-absolutely-flat-over-field, and Algebra Tag 00U3, lemma-etale-over-field

proof.text: An embedding $F\to K^s$ exists. Indeed, by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique](1) choose an algebraic closure $L/F$. It is also an algebraic closure of $K$. Here is the algebraicity check: for $z\in L$, the finitely many coefficients of a monic equation for $z$ over $F$ lie in a finite extension $K_0/K$ (adjoin these finitely many algebraic elements). If the equation has degree $m$, the $K_0$-span of $1,z,\ldots,z^{m-1}$ is closed under multiplication by $z$. Using a finite $K$-basis of $K_0$, its finite $K$-dimension yields a nonzero polynomial over $K$ vanishing at $z$. Thus $L/K$ is algebraic, and $L$ is algebraically closed by construction. Apply [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique](2) over $K$ to obtain $L\simeq\Omega$. The image of $F$ lies in $K^s$, because $F/K$ is separable algebraic and [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure] describes $K^s$ as precisely those separable algebraic elements of $\Omega$. Restricting this embedding to $B$ and taking spectra gives the required specialization.

source.place: Tags 09GT/09GV, theorem-existence-algebraic-closure and lemma-algebraic-closures-isomorphic; elementary finite-coefficient algebraicity argument supplied here

proof.text: Let $t,t'$ correspond to embeddings $i,i':F\to K^s\subset\Omega$ as in Step 2. View $\Omega$ as an $F$-extension separately through $i$ and through $i'$. In either case it is an algebraic closure of $F$: it is algebraically closed, and a polynomial over $K$ for an element of $\Omega$ remains a polynomial over the embedded copy of $F$. By [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique](2), now over $F$, there is a field isomorphism $a:\Omega\to\Omega$ satisfying $a\circ i=i'$. Both embeddings fix $K$, so $a$ fixes $K$. It preserves $K^s$ by its defining separability property [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Let $\sigma$ be the corresponding automorphism of $\bar\eta$ (and use its induced automorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}K^s$). On rings $(t\circ\sigma)^\#=a\circ i|_B=i'|_B=(t')^\#$; hence $t'=t\circ\sigma$. This proves transitivity without assuming the intermediate extension $F/K$ is normal.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.8, printed p. 277: the conjugating generic geometric isomorphism; its field argument is supplied using Stacks 09GV

proof.text: For an $s$-automorphism $\tau$ of $\bar s$, its field map $\tau^\#:\Xi\to\Xi$ preserves $k^s$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] with base ring $A$, source algebra $B$, target henselian local ring $B$, prime $\mathfrak m_B$, and residue map $\tau^\#|_{k^s}$. All hypotheses hold by Step 1. It gives a unique local $A$-map $h:B\to B$ inducing that residue map. Applying the same result to $\tau^{-1}$ and then its uniqueness to the two composites proves $h$ is an automorphism. This is the induced action of $\tau$ on the strict localization: on every pointed etale neighbourhood its map is uniquely determined by the prescribed residue embedding, by the same uniqueness assertion. The composite $\tau\circ t$ therefore has ring map $t^\#\circ h$, so is again a specialization to $\bar s$. Applying Step 4 to $t$ and this specialization gives $\sigma$ with $\tau\circ t=t\circ\sigma$, as required.

source.place: Tag 08HR, lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit; application to the strict henselization with its fixed residue embedding

proof.text: Finally let the two chosen generic geometric points be $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_1$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_2$, where each $\Omega_j$ is an algebraic closure of $K$. Given specializations $t_j$, Step 2 gives embeddings $i_j:F\to\Omega_j$ whose images lie in the respective separable closures. Each $\Omega_j$, regarded through $i_j$, is an algebraic closure of $F$ by the polynomial argument of Step 4. By [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique](2) over $F$, choose $a:\Omega_1\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_2$ with $a i_1=i_2$. It fixes the common $K$ and identifies the separable closures by [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Thus its spectrum $\sigma:\bar\eta_2\to\bar\eta_1$ satisfies $t_2=t_1\circ\sigma$. Applying this also with $t_2$ replaced by $\tau\circ t_2$ proves the closed-automorphism compatibility for different choices. Existence for each choice was already proved in Step 3.
